tone_statements.citation: Mendes Júnior, Djalma Gomes. 2007. Comparação fonológica do Kuruáya com o Mundurukú. Dissertação de Mestrado (Linguística), Universidade de Brasília, Brasília. 66 pp.http://repositorio.unb.br/handle/10482/3108
tone_statements.quote: O Mundurukú e o Kuruáya são línguas tonais. Braun & Crofts (1965) reconheceram quatro tons em Mundurukú: ‘alto’, ‘médio’, ‘baixo’ e ‘laringalização’. Entretanto, Picanço (2005:12) reconhece um sistema de apenas dois tons contrastivos: ... Para o Kuruáya, Costa (1998), mesmo sem apresentar um estudo mais detido sobre o sistema tonal do Kuruáya, verifica a existência de dois tons. Em seu estudo, apresenta apenas dois pares tonais contrastivos: ... Em nossa base de dados, foram encontrados dois possíveis pares tonais contrastivos, entretanto não dispomos dos exemplos com uma análise tonal.
tone_statements.translation: Mundurukú and Kuruáya are tone languages. Braun & Crofts (1965) recognised four tones in Mundurukú: 'high', 'mid', 'low' and 'laryngealisation'. However, Picanço (2005:12) recognises a system of only two contrastive tones: ... For Kuruáya, Costa (1998), even without presenting a more detailed study of the Kuruáya tone system, finds the existence of two tones. In his study he presents only two contrastive tonal pairs: ... In our database two possible contrastive tonal pairs were found; however, we do not have the examples with a tonal analysis.
tone_statements.summary: 2 tones (high '1' vs low '2' in Costa's notation) asserted after Costa 1998; 2 published minimal pairs + 2 unanalysed candidate pairs; analysis explicitly preliminary.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim at the stated locator (Costa 2002 p. 97, sec. 4) in the PDF we hold/scanned, and the Silva 2009 p. 47 endorsement verified in the text we hold. (2) The deciding source is the primary phonological description of the language (Costa 1998/2002), and every other first-hand description that exists and touches prosody — Mendes 2007 p. 49 and Silva 2009 p. 47, both from separate fieldwork traditions (UnB/Rodrigues and UFPA/Picanço) — states or endorses invariable final stress; none reports weight sensitivity, lexical exceptions or secondary stress. Picanço 2005 and Nimuendajú 1930 are silent on the rule. sources.quote: No Kuruaya stress/prosody study found beyond the held Costa 1998/2002, Mendes 2007, Silva 2009, Picanço 2005. Picanço's Kuruaya-related DOIs are Picanço 2010 IJAL (nasal harmony in Proto-Mundurukú) only; Picanço & Baraúna 2013 (Bol. Mus. Goeldi) per CrossRef abstract treats Asuriní do Xingu, Wayampí and Mundurukú, not Kuruaya.
